findings.evidence: features/006-insights-skill/006-insights-skill-prd.md:AC-16 — AC-16 verifies the chat-line summary on successful runs and names five resolved tokens (N corpus size, C clusters surfaced, P proposals, A accepted count, R rejected count, D deferred count where deferred = proposals the user neither accepted nor rejected at this run). The 'D deferred' concept appears in AC-16 AND in the runs.jsonl Schema Appendix's `promotions_deferred: 0` line, but no R-level requirement establishes how a proposal becomes 'deferred' — neither R8 (three-option user prompt: accept-and-write, edit-and-write, reject) nor any other R names a fourth path that produces the deferred state. R8 is binary at the user prompt level: every proposal must reach a `1|2|3` choice; auto-default is a failed run. AC-8 enforces this: 'Empty input or any input not matching `1|2|3` re-prompts. The skill exits with a failed run if it auto-defaults.' So a successful run cannot have any deferred proposals — every proposal is necessarily accepted, edited, or rejected. The 'deferred' counter in AC-16 + the Schema Appendix verifies a state the R-level requirements do not establish. Reverse traceability fails: AC-16's deferred-count clause is an orphan AC clause (per goal-driven-reviewer.md anti-pattern: 'An AC that doesn't verify any stated R. Reverse traceability: every AC must trace to ≥1 R').
findings.claim: Coverage gap (orphan AC clause, reverse traceability failure under E4) — AC-16 + the runs.jsonl Schema Appendix track a `promotions_deferred` count for a state ('user neither accepted nor rejected at this run') that no R-level requirement establishes. R8 + AC-8 together specify a binary user-prompt outcome: every proposal must be accepted, edited, or rejected; auto-default is a failed run. The deferred state has no path to existence in v1. Goal-Driven Execution principle's reverse traceability: every AC must trace to ≥1 R. The architectural intent (proposals can persist across runs without forcing a binary call this month) may be correct, but the PRD body has no R-level expression of the deferral mechanism. Downstream `specflow:test` building a test plan against this PRD would not have an R to bind the test case to; the test would be testing a counter for a state the skill never produces.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) add a new requirement R{new} that explicitly establishes the deferral mechanism: 'R{new}. Deferred proposals carry across within-month re-runs. When a user has not yet accepted or rejected a proposal AND the user explicitly elects to defer (via a fourth user-prompt option, or by exiting the run before resolving every proposal), the proposal is recorded in the active report's `proposed-deferred` section and re-surfaces on the next within-month re-run. The deferred count appears in the runs.jsonl `promotions_deferred` field. Cross-month rollover drops deferred proposals (they're re-evaluated against the new month's corpus).' AND extend R8 to add the fourth option AND extend AC-8 to drop the 'auto-default is a failed run' clause for the deferral path; OR (b) drop the `promotions_deferred` counter from AC-16 and the runs.jsonl Schema Appendix entirely (AC-16's chat-line becomes 4 tokens not 5; the runs.jsonl shape drops the deferred line). Option (a) preserves the architectural intent at R-level; option (b) is the surgical edit removing the orphan claim. Recommend option (b) — the within-month re-run replace-the-active-report semantic per R11 already lets users defer implicitly by NOT running the report-render loop until ready; an explicit deferral mechanism duplicates that existing path. Removing the deferred counter sharpens the chat-line and removes the orphan clause.

findings.evidence: features/006-insights-skill/006-insights-skill-prd.md:AC-1 — AC-1 verifies that the report contains a `## Field-shape clusters` section AND a `## Token-frequency clusters` section, listing every cluster with `len(unique_contributing_ids) >= 3`. The verify step is binary at the section-existence level: 'The report's body contains a `## Field-shape clusters` section listing every (lane_assigned, ai_assistance_level, blast_radius_outcome) tuple bucket where `len(unique_contributing_ids) >= 3` AND a `## Token-frequency clusters` section.' But the binary check has a soft edge: when a corpus has zero clusters above the threshold (corpus large enough to pass R10's minCorpusSize check but pattern-sparse enough that no field-shape tuple or n-gram clusters reach 3 contributing ids), what does AC-1 expect? The current wording implies the sections must be present with whatever clusters exist (even zero), but doesn't say so explicitly. A fresh agent verifying AC-1 against an empty-cluster report could read it two ways: (1) sections present, lists empty (binary pass — sections exist); (2) sections present with no clusters listed is a failed render because 'every cluster' implies ≥1 cluster (binary fail — no clusters). 'Every cluster' is the kind of phrase that fails the binary test under Goal-Driven's lens question.
findings.claim: Soft verification — AC-1's 'listing every cluster' phrasing is ambiguous on the empty-cluster case. Goal-Driven principle's binary test: 'Could a fresh agent run this step in isolation and tell me unambiguously whether it passed?' A fresh agent reading AC-1 on an empty-cluster report would not know whether to pass or fail. The empty-cluster case is a real path (corpus has 12 entries, none of the field-shape tuples or n-grams reach 3 distinct contributing ids — the report should still be produced per R11's replace-in-place semantic, but AC-1 is silent on its shape).
findings.proposed_change: Edit AC-1 to explicitly handle the empty-cluster case: 'The report's body contains a `## Field-shape clusters` section AND a `## Token-frequency clusters` section. Each section lists every cluster with `len(unique_contributing_ids) >= 3`; when zero clusters meet the threshold for a section, the section's body contains the literal sentinel: "No clusters above the 3-observation threshold this run." Sections are always present (even when empty); a report missing either section header is a failed render.' This makes the empty-cluster case binary: section header present + sentinel body or section header present + cluster list. A fresh agent can verify pass/fail unambiguously.
